title: Attention Sparsity is Input-Stable: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation via Offline Sparsity Profiling and Online QK Co-Clustering
claim: Layer-wise sparsity is an intrinsic property that stays nearly identical across different inputs but varies strongly across layers.
layout: 4 line-plot panels in 2x2 grid, shared legend on top
description: A 2x2 grid of line plots under one shared legend bar listing five colored lines, Input 1 to Input 5 (teal, red, yellow, blue, green). Each panel is titled with a video model: Wan2.1-14B-T2V, Wan2.1-14B-I2V, Wan2.2-A14B-T2V and HunyuanVideo-T2V. The x-axis is layer index, running 0 to 40 for the Wan models and 0 to 60 for HunyuanVideo. The y-axis is attention density from 0 to 1. In every panel the five curves almost overlap, so the density profile barely changes with input. Density varies a lot across layers. In the Wan models it dips to about 0.2 in the middle layers and rises toward 0.8 near the end. HunyuanVideo stays near 0 with spikes in the last layers. The eye goes to the tight bundle of lines.
caption: An example acceleration comparison on the Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B [ref]. All experiments are conducted on a single NVIDIA H200 GPU at a 720p resolution with 81 frames.
abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) achieve strong video generation quality but suffer from high inference cost due to dense 3D attention, motivating sparse attention techniques for improving efficiency. However, existing training-free sparse attention methods for video generation still face two unresolved limitations: ignoring layer heterogeneity in attention pruning and ignoring query-key coupling in block partitioning, which hinder a better quality-speedup trade-off. In this work, we uncover a critical insight: attention sparsity is an intrinsic layer-wise property, with only minor variation across different inputs. Motivated by this observation, we propose SVOO, a training-free sparse attention framework for fast video generation via offline layer-wise sparsity profiling and online bidirectional co-clustering. Specifically, SVOO adopts a two-stage paradigm: (i) offline layer-wise sensitivity profiling to derive intrinsic per-layer pruning levels, and (ii) online block-wise sparse attention via a bidirectional co-clustering algorithm. Extensive experiments on seven widely used video generation models demonstrate that SVOO achieves a superior quality-speedup trade-off over state-of-the-art methods, delivering up to 1.93x speedup while maintaining a PSNR of up to 29 dB on Wan2.1. Code is available at: https://github.com/Mutual-Luo/SVOO.
